title: My Ideal Travel Plan

prepTasks.word: I'm going to make the most of...

writingModel: My Ideal Travel Plan: Five Days in Georgia — by Daniyar Bekmuratov

I have been thinking about this trip for over a year, and this summer I'm finally going to make it happen. I'm going to spend five days in Tbilisi, Georgia — a city I have read about, watched documentaries about, and heard described by everyone who has been there as one of the most beautiful places they have ever visited.

I'm flying from Almaty to Tbilisi on the 15th of June. The flight takes about four hours. I've already booked my ticket — I bought it three months ago when the price was at its lowest. I'll arrive in Tbilisi in the evening and take a taxi from the airport to my hostel. The hostel is in the old town district, which means I'll be within walking distance of most of the main sights.

My plan for the five days is this: Day 1 — arrive and explore the old town on foot, following no particular route and stopping wherever looks interesting. Day 2 — visit the Narikala Fortress and the famous Sulphur Baths. Day 3 — take a day trip to Mtskheta, the ancient capital of Georgia, which is only 20 kilometres from Tbilisi. Day 4 — spend the morning in the National Museum and the afternoon in the Marjanishvili district, which I've heard has excellent cafés. Day 5 — pack my bags in the morning, walk slowly through the city one last time, and take the evening flight home.

I'm going to travel light — just a backpack with five days' worth of clothes, a camera, and my notebook. I've booked the hostel dormitory, which costs around 20 dollars per night. My daily budget for food and transport is around 25 dollars — Georgia is known for being affordable, and the food is apparently extraordinary.

I'm most looking forward to the food, honestly. Georgian cuisine — khinkali, khachapuri, churchkhela — is famous across the former Soviet Union, and I want to try as many dishes as possible. I've read that the best restaurants are small, family-run places that don't appear on any tourist map. I'm going to find them.

This trip is going to be everything I've hoped for — and probably a few things I haven't anticipated. That's the point. I'll set off in June, make the most of every day, and come back with a full notebook and an empty wallet. I can't wait.
